item.title: Holomorphic flexibility properties of strongly commuting varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.05905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study holomorphic flexibility properties of the strongly commuting variety of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$. We prove that the smooth locus of the strongly commuting variety of $G$ is Oka-$1$. We also prove that the smooth locus of the commuting variety of a semisimple complex Lie algebra is Oka-$1$, and that it contains a Zariski dense open subset which is algebraically elliptic.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Giannini

item.title: Entire solutions of a special binomial differential equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the binomial differential equation $$ ff'-a(f'')^2=be^{2c},$$ where $a(z)$, $b(z)$, $c(z)$ are polynomials such that $b(z)\not\equiv 0$ and $c(z)$ is non-constant. In this paper, we determine all entire solutions of this equation.
item.dc:creator: Dong-hai Zhao, Jie Zhang, Liang-wen Liao

item.title: A property of boundary extensions of atomic singular inner functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.06877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a property of the Hilbert transform, we prove a measure theoretic result concerning the extensions of atomic singular inner functions to the circle. Various alternative proofs are presented using the mean value theorem for harmonic functions and a well-known property of Blaschke products. Using the main result, we establish several facts concerning atomic singular inner functions and their logarithms.
item.dc:creator: Iason Efraimidis, Adrian Llinares, Sullivan MacDonald, Ignacio Uriarte-Tuero, Dragan Vukotic

item.title: Gromov hyperbolicity and uniformity
item.description: arXiv:2611.05416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we first exhibit an example which answers negatively to a question posed by Herron et al. in 2008. That is, there is a rectifiably connected open set in a proper geodesic metric space so that it is Gromov hyperbolic with respect to the quasihyperbolic metric, and its Gromov boundary endowed with a visual metric is naturally bilipschitz equivalent to its metric boundary, but it is not uniform. Moreover, two positive answers are given under additional hypotheses. It is shown that a metric space is uniform if and only if it is Gromov hyperbolic and the natural map between its Gromov closure and its metric completion exists and satisfies a relatively quasisymmetric condition. Both bounded and unbounded cases are in our considerations via two different uniformization theorems developed recently by Bonk et al. and the first author, respectively. Finally, we characterize uniform metric spaces with uniformly perfect boundaries in terms of Gromov hyperbolicity and Teichm\"uller's displacement property.
item.dc:creator: Qingshan Zhou

item.title: Odd and even fake quadrics isogenous to a product
item.description: arXiv:2611.06077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A $\mathbb{Q}$-homology quadric is a smooth compact complex surface which has the same $\mathbb{Q}$-homology as a quadric surface, that is, the product of two $2$-dimensional spheres. It is called fake if it is minimal and not rational. Among them are the fake quadrics which are isogenous to a product of complex curves. In this paper, we determine the parity of the intersection forms of all fake quadrics isogenous to a product of unmixed type. In particular, we show that there are fake quadrics with odd intersection forms.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Catanese, JongHae Keum, Do Geun Kim, Kyoung-Seog Lee

item.title: Equilibrium webs and stability for arbitrary families of endomorphisms of projective spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.06211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider arbitrary holomorphic families of endomorphisms of a complex projective space. We prove that the existence of an equilibrium web implies the holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles contained in the Julia set, i.e., the support of the unique measure of maximal entropy. Together with previous results of Berteloot, Bianchi, Br\'evard, Buff, and Dupont, this completes the extension of the stability-bifurcation theory to arbitrary families of holomorphic endomorphisms. The same conclusions also hold for holomorphic families of polynomial-like maps of large topological degree.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Bianchi, Zhuchao Ji, Junyi Xie

item.title: Evolution Dynamics and Cauchy Problems with Quaternionic Variables and Lifting to Banach Bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.06721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop a theory of evolution dynamics in a Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-algebra and establish a well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problem of evolution equations with quaternionic variables. First, we study the geometric properties of slice structures of Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-modules. By employing different slice structures, we construct some noncommutative Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-subalgebras which are compatible with the slice regularity of the functions involved. Moreover, through the quaternionic sliced geometric path integral over Banach bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-module, an integral representation of the solution to the homogeneous Cauchy problem with quaternionic variables is obtained in a quaternionic $\sigma$-ball, and for the first time, a local existence and uniqueness theorem is established for $\sigma$-analytic solutions. Then the local $\sigma$-analytic solution is extended to the entire quaternionic spherical sectorial region, thereby proving a global existence and uniqueness theorem for the Cauchy problem. Based on it, the notion of an evolution system in a quaternionic $\mathbb{H}$-algebra is introduced and its core properties are established. In addition, the global existence and uniqueness theorems are obtained under hyperbolic-like and parabolic-like conditions. Finally, the structure of Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-modules and $\mathbb{H}$-algebras is lifted to Banach bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-modules and $\mathbb{A}$-algebras, and a well-posedness theory for evolution equations in this setting is developed. This reveals, from a new perspective, the universality of well-posedness for the Cauchy problem under the generic noncommutative $\mathbb{A}$-algebraic structures.
item.dc:creator: Chao Wang, Guangzhou Qin, Jibin Li

item.title: Distance-Weighted Norm Equivalences for Analytic Functions on John Domains
item.description: arXiv:2608.23940v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$ be a bounded John domain and set $\delta(z)=\text{dist}(z,\partial\Omega)$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $\alpha>\text{dim}_A(\partial\Omega)-2$, we establish a norm equivalence between $\int_\Omega |g|^p\delta^\alpha\,dA$ and $\int_\Omega |g'|^p\delta^{\alpha+p}\,dA$ for analytic functions $g$ on $\Omega$, with a point-evaluation term fixing the additive constant. The estimate of the derivative term is local and holds on every proper planar domain, whereas the converse follows from a distance-weighted Poincar\'e inequality on John domains. Taking $\alpha=mp-2$ yields the corresponding comparison between the $m$-th and $(m+1)$-st derivatives. For $m\ge2$ the boundary-dimension condition is automatic, so the only dimension-sensitive case is the comparison between $\int_\Omega |f'|^p\delta^{p-2}\,dA$ and $\int_\Omega |f''|^p\delta^{2p-2}\,dA$ when $1<p<2$. We show that this restriction is sharp within the class of quasidisks by using self-similar Rohde snowflakes. We also construct, for every $s>1$, an inward-cusp $s$-John domain on which the comparison fails, showing that the ordinary John condition cannot in general be weakened.
item.dc:creator: Katsuhiko Matsuzaki, Huaying Wei

item.title: Entire solutions of Fermat-Type Partial Differential-Difference equations in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01931v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the finite-order entire solutions of the following Fermat-type partial differential-difference equations: \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z+c))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z+c)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \left(\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_1}+\left(P_1(z)f(z+c)+P_2(z)f(z)\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} in $\mathbb{C}^m$, where $m_1,m_2\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $m_1+m_2>2$, $c=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_m)\in\mathbb{C}^m$, $P(\not\equiv 0)$, $P_1$, $P_2$ and $Q_i\;(i=1,2,\ldots,m)$ are polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^m$ such that $P(z)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{C}^m$. The results established in this paper generalize those of Xu et al. \cite{Xu-Luo-Cao-2025} from $\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathbb{C}^m$.
item.dc:creator: Sujoy Majumder, Jhilik Banerjee, Abhijit Banerjee, Elias Saleeby

item.title: Loewner evolution driven by complex Brownian motion (with simulations by Minjae Park)
item.description: arXiv:2203.07313v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Loewner evolution whose driving function is $W_t = B_t^1 + i B_t^2$, where $(B^1,B^2)$ is a pair of Brownian motions with a given covariance matrix. This model can be thought of as a generalization of Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) with complex parameter values. We show that our Loewner evolutions behave very differently from ordinary SLE. For example, if neither $B^1$ nor $B^2$ is identically equal to zero, then the set of points disconnected from $\infty$ by the Loewner hull has non-empty interior at each time. We also show that our model exhibits three phases analogous to the phases of SLE: a phase where the hulls have zero Lebesgue measure, a phase where points are swallowed but not hit by the hulls, and a phase where the hulls are space-filling. The phase boundaries are expressed in terms of the signs of explicit integrals. These boundaries have a simple closed form when the correlation of the two Brownian motions is zero.
item.dc:creator: Ewain Gwynne, Joshua Pfeffer

item.title: On the Existence, Smoothness, and Order-Two Entire Extension of the Navier-Stokes Equations in Critical Fourier-Besov Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2405.07929v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish global existence, smoothness, and physical energy bounds for solutions to the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \ge 3$) under a scaling-critical smallness condition in the homogeneous Fourier-Besov spaces $\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, defined as the weak space $F \dot{B}^{\frac{d}{p'}-1}_{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$ and $F \dot{B}^{-1}_{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ at the endpoint $p = 1$. By combining the nonassociative algebra of Riesz convolutions and spaces of functions dominated by Fourier-Caloric flows $\mathscr{V}(\lambda)$ with a Littlewood-Paley dyadic atomic decomposition, we prove that the Catalan Picard series converges globally whenever $\|\widehat{u^0}\|_{\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)} < C\nu$. This threshold reaches the sharp boundary of well-posedness prior to norm inflation, strictly improves upon the classical Fujita-Kato $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ condition, and admits explicit multiscale Schwartz initial data with arbitrarily large $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $H^k(\mathbb{R}^d)$ norms. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for positive times, the velocity and pressure fields admit an analytic extension to the complex domain $\mathbb{C}^d$, forming a smooth curve of entire vector fields of order two. Finally, for arbitrary initial data outside the critical ball, we employ fractional Riesz convolutions $*_\alpha$ ($0 < \alpha < 1$) to derive an explicit lower bound $T_{\max}(u^0) > 0$ on the lifespan of smooth, order-two entire solutions, establishing a sharp dichotomy between global continuation via viscous re-entry into the critical ball and a scaling-invariant lower blow-up rate.
item.dc:creator: Brian David Vasquez Campos

item.title: Distribution of mixed character sums and extremal problems for Littlewood polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2510.06161v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove distributional results for mixed character sums \begin{equation*}\sum_{n\le x }\chi(n)e(n\theta),\end{equation*} for fixed $\theta\in [0,1]$ and random character $\chi \pmod q$, as well as for a fixed character $\chi$ and randomly sampled $\theta\in [0,1].$ We present various applications of our results. For example, we construct Littlewood polynomials with large Mahler measure and $L_1$ norm, thus establishing new records in the Mahler and Newman problems. We also prove asymptotics for the $L_{2k}$ norms of well-known Turyn polynomials as $k\to\infty$, refuting a conjecture of G\"unther and Schmidt. An important ingredient in our work is a general way of dealing with "log-integrability" problems.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan W. Bober, Oleksiy Klurman, Besfort Shala
